---
title: "Glossary"
description: "Snakemake terms used in the course, each in a sentence or two, with the module that teaches it."
---

Terms are in the order the course introduces them. Each links to the module
that teaches it; the [cheat sheet](cheatsheet.qmd) has the syntax.

::: {.glossary}

Rule
: A recipe for making output files from input files: `input:`, `output:` and
  a `shell:`, `run:` or `script:` that does the work. A rule is a template;
  it does nothing until some target needs its output.
  [Module 1](lessons/01-rules.qmd)

Target
: The file (or rule) you ask Snakemake to produce, on the command line or in
  the first rule of the Snakefile (by convention `rule all`). Snakemake works
  backward from the targets to decide what to run.
  [Module 1](lessons/01-rules.qmd)

Job
: One run of a rule for one set of wildcard values, for example `align` for
  `HCT116_CTCF_1`. A dry run lists the jobs and counts them per rule.
  [Module 1](lessons/01-rules.qmd)

Dry run
: `snakemake -n`: build the DAG, check that inputs exist and print the jobs
  that would run, without running any of them. Do one before every real run.
  [Module 1](lessons/01-rules.qmd)

Wildcard
: A `{name}` in an output path that matches any text, like `{sample}` in
  `output/{sample}/{sample}.bam`. Snakemake fills it in from the file it needs
  and uses the same value in the input and the command.
  [Module 2](lessons/02-wildcards.qmd)

`expand()`
: Builds a list of file names from a pattern and lists of values, for example
  every sample's BAM. Mostly used in `rule all` and other aggregating rules.
  [Module 2](lessons/02-wildcards.qmd)

DAG
: The directed acyclic graph of jobs: which job needs which other job's
  output. `snakemake --dag | dot -Tsvg > dag.svg` draws it;
  `--rulegraph` draws one box per rule instead of per job.
  [Module 2](lessons/02-wildcards.qmd)

Config
: A YAML file of settings (paths, thresholds, which steps to run) read with
  `configfile:` into the `config` dictionary, so nothing that changes between
  runs is written into the rules.
  [Module 3](lessons/03-config.qmd)

Samplesheet
: A table with one row per sample that the Snakefile reads (with pandas) to
  get sample names, files and metadata such as each ChIP sample's control.
  [Module 3](lessons/03-config.qmd)

Input function
: A Python function (or `lambda`) in `input:` that receives the job's
  `wildcards` and returns its input files. Use it when the input depends on a
  lookup, such as the control that belongs to a ChIP sample.
  [Module 3](lessons/03-config.qmd)

`params`
: Values passed to the command that are not files, such as a MAPQ cutoff.
  They can be computed from wildcards or config, and changing them can trigger
  a rerun.
  [Module 4](lessons/04-rules-that-behave.qmd)

`log` and `benchmark`
: Per-job files for the tool's messages (`log:`) and for the time and memory
  the job used (`benchmark:`). Both take wildcards, like outputs.
  [Module 4](lessons/04-rules-that-behave.qmd)

`threads` and `resources`
: How many cores a job uses and what else it needs (memory, runtime). Snakemake
  uses them to fit jobs into `--cores` locally and to request them from the
  scheduler on a cluster.
  [Module 4](lessons/04-rules-that-behave.qmd), [Module 5](lessons/05-cluster.qmd)

Temporary and protected files
: `temp()` marks an output Snakemake deletes once no job needs it (an
  unsorted BAM); `protected()` makes an output read-only so it is not
  overwritten by accident (a reference index).
  [Module 4](lessons/04-rules-that-behave.qmd)

Conda directive
: `conda: "envs/align.yml"` gives a rule its own software environment.
  With `--software-deployment-method conda` (or `--sdm conda`) Snakemake builds
  it once and runs the job inside it.
  [Module 4](lessons/04-rules-that-behave.qmd)

Profile
: A folder with a `config.yaml` of command-line options (executor, number of
  jobs, default resources) for one place where the pipeline runs. Select it
  with `--profile profiles/longleaf`, so the Snakefile stays the same
  everywhere.
  [Module 5](lessons/05-cluster.qmd)

Executor
: The part of Snakemake that starts jobs: the default runs them on this
  machine; the SLURM executor plugin submits each job with `sbatch` and
  watches it.
  [Module 5](lessons/05-cluster.qmd)

Launcher script
: The lab's `<Pipeline>.sh` wrapper: it picks the profile, loads the site's
  software and calls `snakemake` with the right options, and can itself be
  submitted with `sbatch`.
  [Module 5](lessons/05-cluster.qmd)

`include:`
: Pulls another file of rules (`rules/align.smk`) into the Snakefile, so a
  long workflow is split by topic.
  [Module 6](lessons/06-structure.qmd)

Script directive
: `script: "scripts/frip.py"` runs a Python or R script with a `snakemake`
  object that holds the job's input, output, params and log, instead of a
  shell command.
  [Module 6](lessons/06-structure.qmd)

Switch
: A config value (`True`/`False` or a list of steps) that turns a part of the
  pipeline on or off, usually by changing what `rule all` asks for.
  [Module 6](lessons/06-structure.qmd)

`onsuccess` / `onerror`
: Blocks of Python that run once when the whole workflow finishes or fails,
  for example to send an email.
  [Module 6](lessons/06-structure.qmd)

Checkpoint
: A rule whose outputs are not known until it has run (how many chunks, which
  clusters). Rules downstream of it use an input function that asks the
  checkpoint for its outputs, and Snakemake re-evaluates the DAG after it
  finishes.
  [Module 7](lessons/07-beyond-files.qmd)

Scatter-gather
: Split one input into N pieces, process the pieces in parallel, merge the
  results. `scattergather:` and the `scatter`/`gather` helpers set this up
  with N in one place.
  [Module 7](lessons/07-beyond-files.qmd)

Sentinel
: An empty file (`touch()` output, often `name.done`) that records that a
  step finished, when the step's real output is a folder or many files.
  Compare with `directory()`, which makes the folder itself the output.
  [Module 7](lessons/07-beyond-files.qmd)

Dry-run test
: A pytest test that runs `snakemake -n` on a small fixture and checks the job
  counts. Fast, needs no tools, and catches broken rules and samplesheets.
  [Module 8](lessons/08-testing.qmd)

Rerun triggers
: What makes Snakemake decide a job must run again: a missing or older output
  (`mtime`), or changed `params`, `input` set, software environment or code.
  `--list-changes` shows which. See the [cheat sheet](cheatsheet.qmd).
  [Module 4](lessons/04-rules-that-behave.qmd)

Wildcard constraints
: A regular expression that limits what a wildcard may match, for example
  `sample="[^/]+"`, so two rules do not both claim the same file.
  [Module 2](lessons/02-wildcards.qmd)

`ruleorder`
: Tells Snakemake which rule wins when two rules could make the same file.
  [Module 7](lessons/07-beyond-files.qmd)

:::
